name: King Yuri of Goguryeo 유리명왕 (瑠璃明王)
bio: Yuri (瑠璃明王) was the second king of Goguryeo, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, and by the traditional chronology reigned from 19 BC to AD 18. He appears in the Samguk sagi (1145), the oldest surviving Korean history, which records his reign, his move of the capital, and the story of his consorts.

Tradition, preserved in the Samguk sagi, makes him the author of the Song of the Yellow Bird (Hwangjo ga), composed about 17 BC after the loss of his consort Chihui. The attribution is traditional only: the four-line song survives in Classical Chinese and cannot be dated or assigned with certainty.

poems.title: 황조가 黃鳥歌 (Hwangjo ga)
poems.author: King Yuri of Goguryeo 유리명왕 (瑠璃明王)
poems.collection: Samguk sagi (1145), Goguryeo annals, as transcribed on ko.wikisource
poems.source: Samguk sagi (1145), Goguryeo annals; text from ko.wikisource 황조가.
poems.text:
翩翩黃鳥
雌雄相依
念我之獨
誰其與歸
